headline: A city in costume, cookies adults cannot buy and a fried chicken manga

campaigns.did: Before Grand Theft Auto VI came out, Rockstar dressed the real Miami as the game's Vice City. A helicopter lowered a giant pink "Welcome to Vice City" sign onto the Miami Heat's arena, the team was set to play in Vice City jerseys on the eve of release, new murals went up in Wynwood and the 24-hour club E11EVEN became NINE1NINE for the launch party.
campaigns.why: The game is set in a version of a real city, so the city became the media. Each piece is a landmark people already photograph. Adweek, citing Sensor Tower, put preorders past $1.5 billion the day before release.
campaigns.steal: Find the place where your product's world already exists and dress it, with local partners who gain from the attention. A few landmarks done properly beat many scattered placements.

campaigns.did: With Grand Theft Auto VI off limits to younger gamers, the cookie brand made a limited pack reserved for them. It goes on sale at booths in Lotus's stores where bouncers check ID to keep it out of the wrong hands. A QR code behind the label opens a private Discord where top Malaysian gamers share tips for Mobile Legends, PUBG Mobile and EA FC.
campaigns.why: It answers the biggest launch of the year by talking to the people shut out of it. The age check, normally the barrier, becomes the joke and the reward. No results have been published yet.
campaigns.steal: When a big moment excludes part of your audience, make something only they can have. Reversing a familiar rule, here the ID check, turns a small product drop into a story.
